items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 41:1
items.html: It is known that through the illumination of AB-SAG of AK that reaches Atzilut, the Parsas of the second restriction are nullified, and the AHAP that fell from every level to the one beneath it return to the level, together with the lower one that clothes those AHAP. Thus Arich Anpin is then found ascending with the HGT of Atik, which became a head and HBD; and Arich Anpin then receives, through its inclusion in Atik, the stature of the revealed AB, as above, Part 1, Page 442, Item 10, see there. Hence the hairs, which are the garments of the revealed AB, are then found again to become garments for this stature of AB. But after this inclusion and coupling, Arich Anpin descends to its place, and its Mochin are again clothed in the MEM-LAMED-TZADIK of Tzelem, and the revealed AB again goes out in the aspect of a returning surrounding light; see there. Now, this matter of the ascent and inclusion of Arich Anpin in Atik operates every time ZA needs to attain Mochin — that is, in all the levels of ZA during the six thousand years, for the Mochin are not permanent in ZA, as is known. And it was explained above, in Answer 35b, that after the exit of the stature of the revealed AB in the aspect of a returning surrounding light, its garments of the ten Sefirot of reflected light remain after it, being two aspects: hairs and white hairs. From the aspect of the Keter of the reflected light come out the white hairs, and from the aspect of the upper nine Sefirot of the reflected light come out the hairs; see there. Hence these two aspects, hairs and white hairs, are renewed and come out after every ascent of Arich Anpin in Atik, and they are constantly added. And these white hairs, renewed and added after every ascent, also ascend upon the Galgalta of Arich Anpin, upon the aspect of the white hairs that are there. And this is called 'dew,' as in the verse 'for the dew of lights, etc.' And this dew is bestowed upon ZA, as in the verse 'for my head is filled with dew, etc.' For it is added and comes after every coupling and drips upon the head of ZA, and its head is filled from this dew. And this is what the Zohar says there: 'And from that dew that he shakes from his head, which is outside, the dead will be awakened for the world to come' (Idra Rabba, Page 128b; and in the Zohar with the Sulam commentary, Idra Rabba, Item 17). For from this dew, which is added and accumulates through every coupling during the six thousand years, there is gathered that measure of lights sufficient for the revival of the dead; and then ZA shakes that dew from its head all at once, and from that great light the dead arise to resurrection. For it is the light of the primordial Hochma of the revealed AB, which is not revealed except at the end of correction, as is known; and this light of Hochma is the secret of the revival of the dead, for the light of Hochma is called living, as is known. (Part 1, Page 357, Item 129).
